title: Course manifest (course.yaml)
description: The manifest a content repo's course.yaml must satisfy — design doc §6.1. This is the contract between content repos and the platform: an importer (in any language) only needs to produce data that validates against this schema. The optional `degrees` and `badges` blocks (§6.1, §9.2, §9.3) are accepted as of Phase 11; a badge item is defined by schemas/badge.schema.json, which is also the contract the admin UI's export-to-YAML action produces.

schema.description: Manifest format version. Fixed at 1 for the lifetime of this schema.

slug.description: Globally-unique course handle (unique across every imported repo). Referenced by degrees, so it cannot be repo-local.

tracks.description: Max 5 tracks — one hue each, from the fixed 5-hue palette.

degrees.description: Degrees declared by this curriculum repo (design §6.1, §9.2). Courses are referenced by GLOBAL slug, so a degree may span repos — and a degree naming a course this instance has not imported is recorded as unsatisfiable rather than failing the import (design §8: "cross-repo references never fail an import").

badges.description: Badges declared by this curriculum repo — the git-sourced half of design §9.3's two sources. The importer REFUSES to overwrite an admin-created badge with the same slug rather than clobbering a hand-tuned one.

required.description: Course slugs that must ALL be complete.

electives.description: `choose: N` out of `from: [slugs]`. `choose` may not exceed the size of `from` — a degree nobody could ever earn is a manifest bug.

id.description: Stable track key, referenced by a lesson's frontmatter `track:` field.

hue.description: The one hue this track owns. Rejecting anything outside this set is what keeps many courses looking like one system (design §6.1) — also enforced as a database CHECK constraint on the `tracks` table, not only here.

id.description: Stable module key, unique within the course.

lessons.description: Repo-relative paths to lesson markdown files, in the order they should be presented — order lives here, not in filenames (design §6.1).
